messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Monitoring: multiple external DNS probes failing for us-east-1 and eu-west-1. symptom=probe_signal_loss, affected_checks=external-dns-lookup, severity=warning :rotating_light:
jamie (oncall): ack. seeing a spike in 502s from the hosted API in us-east-1 too. customers pinging support. linking the dashboard: https://console/redwood/metrics/probes?region=us-east-1
ben (network): pulling traces. early look — we have intermittent NXDOMAINs and long DNS latencies hitting our egress proxies for a subset of AZs in us-east-1. possible DNS resolver path issue.
sasha (eng-sre): is telemetry missing from the probe runner or are probes returning explicit errors? need to know if this is monitoring-only or real user impact.
jamie (oncall): probes show failures + monitor ingestion gap for ~3m starting at 12:03UTC. API error-rate increase started ~12:05UTC. looks correlated.
ben (network): running quick dig to our customer-facing domain via the affected egress IPs:
```
dig @8.8.8.8 example-cust.redwood-inference.com +time=2 +tries=1
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, id: 12345
;; flags: qr rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0, AUTHORITY: 1, ADDITIONAL: 1
;; AUTHORITY SECTION: example-cust.redwood-inference.com. 30 IN SOA ns1 ...
```
ben (network): notice the SOA TTL is 30s for some responses and NXDOMAIN for others. looks like inconsistent authoritative behavior or a transient authoritative zone issue.
lorenzo (infra): cross-region routing (BGP) in us-east-1 shows brief egress path churn around 12:02UTC (route flap table). I suspect some upstream provider had a partial outage, our resolvers rebalanced and a few queries hit stale NS.
jamie (oncall): customer impact: a subset of requests to hosted API in us-east-1 got 502/504s and a few LBs retried causing tail latency. I put a quick note in support: "We are investigating a regional DNS/egress issue affecting some requests in us-east-1 and eu-west-1."
pagerduty: Incident assigned to jamie (oncall). Paging escalation to network oncall: ben.
ben (network): I'm temporarily routing probe traffic to an alternate resolver pool to see if failures stop. doing config tweak on probe-agent: `PROBE_RESOLVERS=["10.0.10.5","10.0.10.6"]` -> `PROBE_RESOLVERS=["10.0.20.5","10.0.20.6"]`
jamie (oncall): done. also increased alert suppression for external-dns-lookup by 2m to avoid cascade alerts while we triage.
sasha (eng-sre): can we confirm customer DNS lookups (live traffic) also hit the same resolvers? we need to know if this is just monitoring infra or customer-facing.
ben (network): checked NAT gateway logs — live egress for some instances resolved via the affected AS path. switched a subset to alternative NATs. initial metrics: probe failures dropped to baseline in the next 60s.
lorenzo (infra): but metrics ingestion from probe agents still shows a 90s gap for some agents (missing telemetry). looks like the probe agent's telemetry exporter timed out against our metrics endpoint during the route churn.
jamie (oncall): action list so far: (1) reroute probes to alternate resolvers (done) (2) route subset of customer egress via alt NATs (done) (3) suppress noisy alerts (done) (4) collect packet captures from affected AZs (ben)
ben (network): pcap attached to thread (uploaded). sample shows repeated truncation of DNS responses and TCP resets to resolver IPs during the window.
sasha (eng-sre): since monitoring ingestion gap existed, some alerts were false-positive of downstream service errors. however we did see real 502s caused by DNS lookup failures. so both monitoring false positives and genuine customer impact. need clear postmortem classification.
jamie (oncall): I'm going to open an incident doc and mark severity=sev2 for now. starting timeline in the doc.
tayla (oncall-next): I'll take over in 35m. please leave a handoff with current state and next steps.
jamie (oncall): handing off to tayla in 35m. current state: traffic rerouted, probe failures decreased, metric ingestion gap resolved for most agents but ~7 agents still missing telemetry. customer facing 502 rate back to baseline. create follow-ups: force-refresh DNS cache TTL to 60s for our edge resolvers, coordinate with upstream provider for root cause, and replace flaky NATs.
ben (network): creating ticket to upstream provider with trace and pcap. preliminary upstream response: "we saw transients on peering — investigating".
lorenzo (infra): we'll also add a synthetic check that validates both DNS authority consistency and TTL monotonicity (detect authoritative servers returning inconsistent SOA/TTL) to avoid this noisy signature in future.
sasha (eng-sre): for now revert the probe heuristic that treats any probe_agent ingestion gap as immediate service outage; change rule to require data-plane errors (e.g., 5xx) in tandem. I'll push a quick monitoring rule change:
```
alert: ExternalDNSFailure
if: (external-dns-lookup_errors > 5) and (probe_agent_heartbeat_recent == true)
for: 2m
```
sasha (eng-sre): that should reduce false positives when telemetry is missing.
jamie (oncall): handoff summary for tayla: root cause suspected upstream egress/DNS path churn causing inconsistent authoritative responses and probe telemetry exporter timeouts. mitigation done: alternate resolvers & NATs, alert damping, probe reroute. outstanding: upstream RCA, 7 probe agents missing telemetry to investigate, postmortem + customer comms draft.
tayla (oncall-next): ack, taking it. I'll own the RCA sync and coordinate customer communication. please add any notes to the incident doc.
ben (network): FYI — also found a small bug in probe-agent exponential backoff that doubled timeout when exporter returns 504; patch queued.
jamie (oncall): thanks all. created post-incident ticket: INC-177999. assigning sasha for monitoring rule changes, ben for upstream comms, lorenzo for infra replacements.
incident-bot: Incident INC-177999 created and linked: https://incidents/redwood/INC-177999
sasha (eng-sre): quick note for the postmortem: classify this as a mixed-impact — monitoring false positives due to telemetry gaps + genuine DNS-induced user errors. action items: improve heartbeat resilience, add authoritative-consistency check, and tighten probe-agent telemetry retries.
ben (network): +1. adding pcap and traces to the incident doc.
jamie (oncall): closing live thread — handoff complete. will watch the ticket until tayla confirms handoff closed. :white_check_mark:
